current_disclosures.section: RISKS RELATED TO OUR OPERATING BUSINESSES
current_disclosures.summary: Qualcomm’s revenues, cash flows, and margins are significantly impacted by customer purchasing timing, product development cycles, and the concentration of device share among a few companies. Declines in premium-tier device sales, shifting consumer demand to refurbished devices, and the resulting pricing power of OEMs may lead to lower prices and reduced revenue contributions from premium integrated circuit products. Engineering efforts to incorporate customer feedback may not result in purchase commitments or recoverable costs, while delays in significant purchases further reduce revenues and available cash resources.

comparisons.peer_topic: Arm ecosystem and R&D investment risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Increased adoption of Arm-based semiconductor designs could lead to further growth of the Arm ecosystem, while AMD may face delays or disruptions in R&D efforts or be required to invest significantly greater resources in R&D than anticipated.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD disclose risks related to the resource intensity and uncertainty of their product development and R&D efforts in response to market or ecosystem changes. Qualcomm states that spending significant engineering and development resources on customer feedback may result in non-recoverable costs or lower purchases than expected. Similarly, AMD warns that increased adoption of Arm-based designs may force it to invest significantly greater resources in R&D than anticipated, or face delays and disruptions in those efforts. Both highlight that the effort to adapt to customer/industry dynamics carries a risk of unrecoverable investment or execution failure.

sentences.text: In addition, we spend a significant amount of engineering and development time, funds and resources in understanding our key customers' feedback and/or specifications and attempt to incorporate such input into our product launches and technologies.

These efforts may not require or result in purchase commitments from such customers or we may have lower purchases from such customers than expected, and consequently, we may not achieve the anticipated revenues from these efforts, or these efforts may result in non-recoverable costs.
Increased adoption of Arm-based semiconductor designs could lead to further growth and development of the Arm ecosystem.
We may also face delays or disruptions in research and development efforts, or we may be required to invest significantly greater resources in research and development than anticipated.

comparisons.peer_summary: Complex products may contain defects, bugs, or reliability issues upon introduction, leading to delays, additional development costs, or recalls. System-wide failures or breaches in customer environments may damage reputation, increase investment costs, and adversely affect financial results if the company is held liable.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm and Broadcom both identify product complexity and the resulting difficulty in predicting customer adoption as a source of financial risk. Qualcomm notes that efforts to incorporate customer feedback may not result in purchase commitments, leading to non-recoverable costs. Broadcom explicitly links product complexity to unforeseen delays, expenses, or defects that can adversely affect market acceptance and damage reputation. Both companies warn that the investment in developing products to meet specific customer requirements carries the risk that the resulting product will not achieve the anticipated commercial success or recover the development costs.

Delays can cause missed customer design windows, larger die sizes, and supply constraints, while new nodes typically have higher depreciation and lower yields than mature nodes.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm and Intel both disclose risks stemming from the uncertainty of customer demand and the potential for unrecoverable costs or revenue shortfalls associated with product development and timing. Qualcomm highlights that efforts to incorporate customer feedback may not result in purchase commitments, leading to lower-than-expected purchases. Intel similarly warns that production timing delays in next-generation nodes can cause the company to miss customer product design windows, resulting in lost revenue opportunities. Both companies emphasize that their investments in technology and product development are contingent on aligning with customer timelines and specifications, with failure leading to financial loss.

comparisons.peer_topic: New product launch timing and component lead-time risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Successful product launches require timely delivery and meeting customer design schedules to secure design wins; long lead-times for some components require ordering up to a year in advance, increasing the risk of excess inventory or lost sales if forecasts vary from actual demand.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm and Micron both highlight the risk that their product development and launch timelines may fail to align with customer needs, leading to lost business opportunities. Qualcomm states that efforts to incorporate customer feedback may not result in purchase commitments. Micron explicitly warns that if it does not meet customer product design schedules or demonstrate functionality well in advance, customers may exclude it from consideration as a supplier. Both disclosures center on the risk that the timing and execution of product development efforts determine whether they secure customer orders or lose them to competitors.
